Forum post — "Strategies for a picky eater?" (Parenting > Toddlers & Preschoolers)

My son Mateo just turned 4 and has been diagnosed with a mild peanut allergy, so we've had to overhaul lunches at his preschool (Little Acorns on Cedar Street). On top of that he's decided he only eats beige food. Any tips from parents who've been through this? I'm happy to swap notes — you can message me here or email carla.m@example.com.

Things that have worked a little: letting him help stir, tiny portions of a new food next to something safe, and not making a big deal when he refuses. Things that haven't: bribery, and hiding vegetables in smoothies (he can always tell).

General advice from our pediatrician that might help others: offer a new food 10-15 times before giving up, and keep mealtimes short and low-pressure.

text:
Forum post — "Returning to work after a long absence" (Careers > Advice)

I'm 46 and returning to work after 18 months off for cancer treatment (I'm in remission now, but still on a maintenance medication that makes mornings rough). Before that I was a senior accountant at Halvorsen & Lowe in downtown Portland, earning about $96k. I've been offered a part-time role at a nonprofit near my home in the Sellwood neighborhood, which would be a big pay cut but a much gentler schedule.

Has anyone made a similar trade-off and regretted it? I'm especially interested in hearing from people who negotiated a phased return rather than choosing between full-time and part-time.

General notes for anyone in the same boat: in the US, the ADA lets you request reasonable accommodations (including a modified schedule), and you don't have to disclose a diagnosis to ask for them.
